Abstract.AbstractText: A 44-year-old female with paraesthesia and pain on the left anterolateral thigh who had been diagnosed with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy by electromyography and muscle biopsy is presented. Neurological examination revealed atrophy of the proximal muscles of both shoulders, plus pseudo hypertrophy of both calves. Electromyography exhibited a myopathic pattern. Musculoskeletal ultrasound imaging demonstrated a fusiform nerve swelling below the inguinal ligament suggesting lateral femoral cutaneous nerve compression, consistent with meralgia paraesthetica. Treatment with a perineural injection of betamethasone dipropionate and betamethasone sodium phosphate combination, and prilocaine-HCl, under ultrasound guidance, was performed. Symptoms resolved within 6 h. At 3-week follow-up, the patient was asymptomatic, and there was no paraesthesia or pain on examination. In this case, ultrasound-guided perineural injection of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve with local anaesthetics and steroid served both diagnostic and therapeutic functions.
